title: Allocator-histogram-drift-oom-timeline
content:
Summary:

Small fleet of serving hosts started experiencing intermittent OOMs during a high-latency customer rollout window (2024-11-05 22:00 - 2024-11-06 03:10 UTC). Root cause appears to be a gradual drift in allocator free-list histograms combined with a workload shift (more long-sequence generation) exposing a fragmentation amplification bug in our modified tcmalloc shim.

Why this doc exists:
- capture timeline & quick wins from oncall
- record hypothesis & short-term mitigations
- propose runbook changes and engineering follow-ups

On-call timeline (high level):
- 22:08 UTC: first alert — host-172.31.42.11 OOM kill, process restart by systemd.
- 22:12 UTC: second host same AZ OOM. Ops oncall @Ravi triaged; pattern looked like host-level mem spike over RSS threshold.
- 22:27 UTC: correlation with a spike in long-sequence requests (client X, rollout flag ramped). Prometheus: sum(rate(requests_total{seq_len>2048}[1m])) increased ~3x.
- 22:35 UTC: heap histograms (allocator.per_size_bucket_count) show increasing count in mid-size buckets (8KB-64KB) and decreasing in small buckets (<1KB) — unexpected drift.
- 23:00 UTC: mitigations applied: rollback of client rollout flag for client X + temporary routing rule to spill long sequences to lower-concurrency pool. Immediate drop in new spike but hosts still unstable.
- 00:40 UTC: discovered large contiguous allocations from KV cache rehydration path — prefetch path recently changed (PR 1860) to allocate scratch buffers per shard instead of reusing arena.
- 01:10 UTC: reproduced locally with stress harness: repeated long-sequence requests + cache rehydrate path led to fragmentation and eventual RSS growth until OOM.
- 03:00 UTC: short-term patch deployed: reuse scratch buffer (hotfix PR 1893) + bump eviction aggressiveness for KV cache to reduce rehydrates under load.
- 03:10 UTC: alerts quieted; continued monitoring.

Observations & data points:
- Hosts that OOMed had active continuous-batching enabled and showed higher batch sizes (~12 average vs baseline 6). That changed allocation shape.
- Allocator telemetry (histograms) drifted over hours: small-bucket counts decreased, medium-bucket increased; free list churn high.
- Native heap fragmentation (mapped but unused memory) was a contributor: jemalloc stats showed "active" >> "allocated" on culprits.
- The cache rehydrate change (PR 1860) allocated many per-shard buffers of ~32KB that lived across requests due to an off-by-one in the reuse path. Under normal load GC/eviction kept them low; under long-seq spike rehydrates increased and eviction lagged, amplifying fragmentation.
- Crash logs: SIGKILL from OOM killer; no coredumps captured (coredump disabled in prod by default).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: allocator free-list / arena reuse bug + workload shift -> fragmentation spiral. Reuse path regression (PR 1860) prevented buffer recycling.
2) Secondary: continuous batching increased peak working set making the fragmentation surface area larger; batching changed allocation lifetimes such that medium buckets retained longer.
3) Tertiary: memory accounting mismatch between runtime and kernel (some host-level background processes) increased pressure; but correlation weaker.

Immediate mitigations taken (during incident):
- Rollback of customer rollout (reduced long-seq traffic).
- Apply routing policy to route long-seq traffic to a separate, lower-concurrency pool (reduces per-host peak).
- Hotfix to reuse scratch buffers (PR 1893) to stop per-request per-shard allocation growth.
- Adjust KV cache eviction policy to be slightly more aggressive for 12h to avoid mass rehydrates.

What worked: 
- Routing change bought time and prevented new hosts from tipping over.
- Hotfix locally repro'd and reduced per-request allocation in stress harness; deployment correlated with drop in allocator histogram drift.

What didn't work / surprises: 
- We had poor visibility into fragmentation until we added jemalloc active/allocated snapshots to dashboard. Need that in default telemetry.
- Coredumps disabled meant no native heap trace after OOM; enabling for select hosts would help but has operational cost.

Data & queries used (examples):
- Prometheus: rate(requests_total{env="prod",seq_len=~">2048"}[1m])
- Alloc hist: allocator_per_size_bucket_count{host=~"host-.*",env="prod"}
- Jemalloc: jemalloc_active_bytes / jemalloc_allocated_bytes by host
- OS free: node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes by host

Repro steps (short):
1) Start serving-runtime in scaled local harness with continuous-batching enabled.
2) Ramp synthetic client that sends sequences with length distribution matching client X (heavy tail to 6k tokens).
3) Force KV cache cold miss and run rehydrate path concurrently across shards.
4) Observe RSS growth via pmap and jemalloc counters; reproduce fragmentation over ~1k iterations.

Short-term runbook updates (to implement now):
- Add jemalloc active/allocated and per-arena counters to default host metrics.
- Add an alert: allocator_active_alloc_ratio > 1.8 for 5m with severity P1 (indicates excessive fragmentation).
- Temporary guardrail: if host sees >2 OOMs in 24h, reduce continuous-batching concurrency to 50% automatically and route long sequences away.
- Add step in oncall playbook: check PRs touching kvcache prefetch/rehydrate or allocator wrappers in last 72h when seeing sudden allocator drift.

Engineering follow-ups / backlog items: (owners assigned)
- [Ravi] formal fix in serving-runtime allocator shim to ensure scratch buffer reuse and audit all per-request allocations (JIRA-ENG-2149).
- [Anya] add jemalloc active/allocated dashboards, per-arena histograms, and example queries to runbook (JIRA-METRICS-110).
- [Theo] stress test harness: integrate long-tail sequence generator and run nightly fragmentation checks against upgraded builds (JIRA-TEST-92).
- [Maya] eval tradeoffs for enabling coredumps on a small canary set of hosts and document retention/rotation policy (JIRA-OPS-57).

Post-incident notes & behavior changes to consider: 
- Batching heuristics should be aware of allocator fragmentation signals; if fragmentation rises, throttle batch consolidation.
- Review all recent changes that altered allocation lifetime shapes (new buffers, moved from stack to heap, per-shard caches).
- Consider opportunistic buffer pooling with size bucketing to limit freelist proliferation.

Open questions: 
- Is the fragmentation primarily due to our allocator shim or is upstream tcmalloc/jemalloc interaction the true root cause? (need bisect with allocator disabled)
- Would enabling periodic madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) on idle arenas reduce resident footprint without impacting perf?
- Are there other customers with long-sequence profiles that might have silently experienced degraded latency but not OOMs? (query to run against request logs)

Action items today (short list):
- Merge and roll hotfix PR 1893 to low-risk pool (DEV-staging), monitor 6h. (Ravi)
- Add jemalloc active/allocated to platform dashboard and create allocator_active_alloc_ratio alert. (Anya)
- Deploy routing guard for long sequences in edge router for 48h as protective measure. (Oncall ops)
- Run targeted query to list all customer rollouts touching seq_len > 2048 in last 7 days and flag owners. (Maya)

Longer-term engineering notes (for design doc):
- Formalize buffer pool abstraction with lifecycle semantics tied to batching window, not per-request.
- Evaluate switching to per-NUMA arena allocation and limiting cross-arena reuse to reduce fragmentation.
- Add offline fragmentation regression test to CI for PRs touching kvcache and batching.

Appendix: quick checklist for next oncall seeing similar symptoms
- Check recent traffic shapes: seq_len distribution, batch_size histogram.
- Pull allocator_per_size_bucket_count for affected hosts and compare to baseline.
- Check jemalloc active/allocated ratio.
- If immediate pressure: route long sequences away and reduce batching concurrency.
- Search for recent PRs touching kvcache prefetch/rehydrate or allocator wrapper libs.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- write small python script to diff histogram snapshots over time and auto-highlight drifted buckets.
- think about making buffer pools language-level (rust typesafe) to avoid off-by-one reuse bugs.

References & links:
- PR 1860 (rehydrate refactor) 
- Hotfix PR 1893 (buffer reuse)
- JIRA-INC-4821 (incident ticket)
- Slack thread: ops-oncall channel thread CK12AB34
